cleanIntro: A Kimber Hunter strips to two pieces for cleaning: rifle and bolt. The bolt comes out past the bolt stop at the left rear of the receiver, and Kimber publishes one step past that — the cocking piece housing unscrews by hand so the inside of the bolt can be cleaned. Nothing else opens.

steps.title: Safety to position 2, finger outside the guard
steps.action: Move the safety to position 2 — the middle position, which blocks the trigger while still allowing the bolt to be worked — and keep your finger outside the trigger guard for everything that follows.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 35pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — OPERATION — Removal of the bolt, printed p.46

steps.title: Magazine out — and it does not unload the rifle
steps.action: Take the magazine out, then open the bolt and look into the chamber and the magazine well. Kimber names this rifle in the warning: removing the magazine alone does not unload it, and a Hunter will fire with the magazine out if a round is chambered.
steps.aside: Open the bolt and confirm the chamber and magazine are unloaded. Do not proceed unless unloaded.
steps.quote: Removing the magazine (Hunter & Tactical Rifles only) alone will not unload the rifle.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 35pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — OPERATION — Removal of the bolt, printed p.46

steps.title: Bolt handle counter-clockwise, bolt to the rear
steps.action: Close the bolt once you have confirmed the rifle is empty, then rotate the handle counter-clockwise to fully open and draw the bolt back. The close-then-open sequence is Kimber's own order and it leaves the extractor where it should be.
steps.quote: Rotate the bolt handle counter-clockwise to the fully open position and slide the bolt to the rear.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 35pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — OPERATION — Removal of the bolt, printed p.46

steps.title: Bolt stop pressed at the left rear — and mind the stock comb
steps.action: Find the bolt stop lever at the left rear of the receiver, push it in, and draw the bolt fully back and out. Guide it clear rather than levering: the bolt passes close to the comb of the stock on the way out and Kimber warns that catching it there marks the wood.
steps.aside: Special care should be taken to not contact the comb of the stock when removing the bolt as cosmetic damage could occur.
steps.quote: While pushing-in the bolt stop lever, pull the bolt fully to the rear and clear of the receiver.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 35pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — OPERATION — Removal of the bolt, printed p.46

steps.title: Field strip complete — and the bolt gets stored separately
steps.action: Rifle and bolt is the whole field strip. Kimber asks that the bolt be kept separate from the rifle while it is being cleaned, serviced, transported or stored — a rifle that cannot chamber a round is the safest thing in a case.
steps.quote: The bolt should be removed from the rifle and stored separately while cleaning, servicing, transporting or storing this rifle.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 35pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — OPERATION — Removal of the bolt, printed p.46

steps.title: Bore guide in, oiled patch from the chamber end
steps.action: Use a bore guide and a quality rod, and start at the chamber — on a bolt rifle the bolt is out, so there is no reason to enter at the muzzle and risk the crown. An oil-soaked patch first to lift the loose fouling.
steps.quote: Using a suitable bore guide and quality cleaning rod, run an oil soaked patch through the barrel starting at the chamber.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 35pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — CARE — Cleaning & Maintenance, printed p.50

steps.title: Chamber, breech face and ejection port wiped dry of solvent
steps.action: Wipe the excess cleaner and lubricant out of the chamber, off the breech face and out of the ejection port. Solvent left in a chamber reaches the next cartridge, and oil that penetrates a primer is a misfire you will blame on the ammunition.
steps.quote: To reduce oil and solvent contamination of cartridges, use a clean patch to remove excess cleaner and lubricant from the chamber, breech face and ejection port.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 35pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — CARE — printed p.51

deepSteps.title: Partial bolt strip only — and it starts with the rifle proven empty
deepSteps.action: Kimber publishes exactly one step past the field strip: the bolt opens far enough to clean inside. Before it does, the same clearing sequence applies — safety at position 2, finger outside the guard, bolt open, chamber and magazine confirmed empty, and the bolt out of the rifle.
deepSteps.aside: If you believe that further disassembly is required, contact Kimber Customer Service or a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: The bolt should only be partially disassembled as outlined in this manual for routine cleaning.
deepSteps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 35pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — OPERATION — Disassembly of the bolt, printed p.37-38

deepSteps.title: Cocking piece housing unscrews counter-clockwise, by hand
deepSteps.action: With the bolt out, unscrew the cocking piece housing counter-clockwise out of the bolt body using your hand — no tools, no vice. That opens the bolt enough to clean the inside of the body and the striker area, which is where old oil and grit gather and slow lock time.
deepSteps.quote: Using your hand, unscrew the cocking piece housing counter-clockwise out of the bolt.
deepSteps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 35pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — OPERATION — Disassembly of the bolt, printed p.37-38

deepSteps.title: Housing back in clockwise, then the bolt back in the action
deepSteps.action: Screw the cocking piece housing clockwise back into the bolt until it is home, then reinstall the bolt in the action the way it came out. That is the end of what Kimber publishes — anything further is Customer Service or a gunsmith.
deepSteps.aside: Insert the bolt back into the action, as described in “Installing the Bolt” section. (see page 45)
deepSteps.quote: Screw the cocking piece housing clock-wise into the bolt.
deepSteps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 35pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — OPERATION — Disassembly of the bolt, printed p.37-38

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bore guide fitted; rod in at the chamber, never the muzzle
Oiled patch first, then solvent and brush, then patches until clean
Light oil to finish; dry patch before shooting

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Body, lugs and bolt face wiped clean
Cocking piece housing off by hand for the inside of the body
Light oil only — this is a rifle, not a machine tool

cleaning.name: CHAMBER & ACTION
tasks: Chamber, breech face and ejection port wiped free of solvent and oil
Bolt raceways in the receiver wiped and lightly oiled

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Bolt stored separately from the rifle
Rust preventative for damp or long-term storage
Clean and lubricate every six months even if unused

reassembly: Cocking piece housing screwed clockwise back into the bolt body.
Bolt head forward into the receiver with the handle up, then pushed fully in.
Bolt handle rotated clockwise to the closed position; work it a few times to prove it runs.
Magazine back in, safety to position 2, then function check before any ammunition.
fncheck: Rifle empty, magazine out, muzzle safe. Reinstall the bolt and work it several times — it should run and lock without drag, and the bolt stop should hold it in the receiver. Check the safety in each position: at position 2 the trigger must be blocked. Then confirm the magazine seats and releases cleanly. If the bolt binds or the safety behaves inconsistently, stop and contact Kimber rather than shooting it.
